That is deliberate, the acceptance criteria named the existing type, so do not rename it on a tidying impulse without checking the card. Also, the repair and the dispatch sweep are serialized in the same \\u0060DispatchLoop\\u0060 task, which is why only \\u0060LeaseHeartbeatService\\u0060 needed the upsert-to-patch fix and \\u0060DispatchEngine.RefreshLocalHeartbeatsAfterSuspensionAsync\\u0060 did not.\\n- Left undone on purpose, three things. The suspension-path upsert above, for the reason in the PR body, and it wants its own card. The board\\u0027s \\u0060PartialHistoryHeld\\u0060 filters in \\u0060TaskStatusComposer\\u0060 and \\u0060IdeaRow\\u0060 still use the old document-based tell, which stays correct because the repair removes the documents those filters read. And the branch is 23 commits behind main, which now carries #257 through #260, so the \\u0060chore: assign Decisions Log #257\\u0060 commit at the tip is stale; that is the mechanical pre-final-pass rebase step\\u0027s job and it will be skipped and reassigned, so do not hand-renumber it.\\n- One thing I noticed but could not pin down: \\u0060PartialReplicatedStreamRepairPlanner.HoldOf\\u0060 re-serializes the applied .NET object rather than the original wire payload, so if a sender\\u0027s payload ever carried a field this build does not know, that field is already gone by the time the repair runs. I do not think it is reachable today and there is nothing to recover it from, but it is worth knowing if a cross-version replication bug ever shows up
